dialog.body: Canvassing Division, this is Walter. Good morning, how can I help you?
Yeah, hello, good morning. Um, I have a question about the voting. I am not sure I understand how it works here, you know.
Sure, I can help with that. Are you registered in Newport already?

Yes, yes, I register, I think two years ago. At the, the car place, the registry. Or maybe I fill a paper, I don't remember. [pause] I am calling because I want to know where is the polling place. Where I go to vote.
Okay. Your polling place depends on which ward and precinct you live in. Do you have your voter card, or the notice that came in the mail?
Hmm, a card. Is a small card? Like a, a white one?
That's usually it, yes. It lists your precinct and the polling location. If you can give me your street address, I can look it up for you.
Ah, no, no, I don't give the address on the phone, sorry. Is the speaker, my wife is here also, I don't want to, you know. Can you tell me just in general?

I understand. I can't name your location without the address, because it's different for each precinct. But you can look it up on the Secretary of State's voter information site, or call back when you have your card in front of you.
Okay, okay. The card, I look for the card. And the other thing, the deadline. There is a deadline, no? For the, for to vote?
There are a few different deadlines, so let me ask. Do you mean the deadline to register, or to request a mail ballot, or are you asking about Election Day itself?
Mail ballot. I think, mail ballot. Because I am planning a trip to see my cousins in Georgia, and I don't know if I am here the day of the election. So I need to vote before, no?
Got it. Which election are you thinking of? Is there a particular date?
Ehh, the next one. The big one. [pause] Is not this month, no? The trip is, um, in the fall, September, maybe October.

Okay. So you'd want to apply for a mail ballot ahead of whichever election falls while you're away. The application has to be received by the board of canvassers a set number of days before that election, and I'd rather give you the exact date once the election is confirmed. Also, there's early in-person voting at City Hall before Election Day, which might work if you leave a little after.
Early voting, in person. At City Hall. So I don't need the mail one, I just go before I travel?
Right, that's an option, as long as you go during the early voting window. Either way works. The mail ballot is just easier if you'll be gone the whole time.
Ah, okay. But the, the mail one, I need a reason? Like I am sick, or something?
No, in Rhode Island you don't need a reason to vote by mail anymore. You just fill out the application and send it in.
No reason. Okay. So, wait, the application, where I get it? Is online or I come there?
Both. You can pick one up here at the office, or I can mail one to you. If you give me your name and mailing address, I'll send it out.
Hmm, the mailing address, again, with my wife here... Can I call another time? I look for the card first, and then I call, and I ask again about the deadline when I know the date.
Of course. We're open weekdays, and you can call back anytime. Have the card handy and we'll sort out the polling place and the application together.
Okay, thank you very much, Walter. I think I understand. More or less. Thank you, bye.
You're welcome. Have a good weekend.
